title: Learning Quadrille Dance Basics | Cayman Islands | Cayman Heritage Guide

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor demonstrates basic steps clearly while text cards provide historical context and instructions. She moves through solo demonstrations and partner work outdoors in a structured sequence.

lesson_structure.note: Instructor introduces herself and the topic
Text screens explain the history and nature of quadrille
Demonstrating move 1: chip step / balance step
Trying steps with a partner holding waist
Partner circle movement using chip step
Final notes on regional differences and costumes

steps_taught.name: The Chip Step / The Balance Step
steps_taught.description: Stepping side to side while manipulating the skirt

steps_taught.name: The Wheel
steps_taught.description: Turning movement typically done with a partner

steps_taught.name: Figure 8
steps_taught.description: Tracing a figure eight pattern with footwork and skirt movement

what_works: Clear text cards introducing each step name
what_hinders: Lack of verbal counting or step-by-step breakdown

quotes.text: So this one is called the chip step or balance step.
The next step would be the wheel which you usually it has to be done with a partner.
Then figure 8. Figure 8 is pretty much what it is, figure 8.

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor demonstrates side-to-side stepping while holding her skirt in an outdoor setting
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact foot placement under the skirt

extraction.distinctive_method: Combining traditional heritage storytelling via on-screen text cards with outdoor solo and partner movement demonstrations.
